title: 1955 London County Council election
summary: Labour retained control of the London County Council, winning 74 of the 126 elected seats. The size of the elected council was trimmed from 129 to 126 for this and the two following elections. Turnout fell to 32.4%.
highlights: Labour holds the LCC with 74 of 126 seats
The elected council is reduced from 129 to 126 members

council.note: 126 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. Seat shares are taken from Rallings & Thrasher's record of LCC results.
council.otherVotesNote: Under the multi-member bloc vote each elector had as many votes as seats to fill; minor-party totals and shares are as recorded in the Elections Centre compendium and contemporary press reports, whose percentage bases differ slightly.

sources.label: Rallings & Thrasher, London County Council Elections 1889–1961 (Elections Centre)
